# Zamborin Games

> A small independent studio building free, instantly-playable games for the browser. Vanilla HTML/JavaScript/Canvas, no engines, no downloads, no logins. Hosted at zamborin.com.

## Games

- [Orbit](https://zamborin.com/orbit/): Ring-spinning light puzzle. Concentric rings carry broken arc-track; spin each ring (drag, or tap to nudge one step) so light runs from the hub out to every bulb on the rim, resolving into a symmetric mandala. A join only carries light when the ring is exactly in true. Later levels gear pairs of rings so turning one turns its partner the opposite way. Scored on level depth and how close to par you finish.
- [Bloom](https://zamborin.com/bloom/): Pipe-rotating irrigation puzzle. Water starts at a tap in the middle of the garden and the ground is tangled with pipes facing the wrong way. Tap a pipe to rotate it 90°; watered pipes turn blue, and a flower opens only once water reaches it. Every board is generated as a connected layout, so a solution always exists.
- [Kaleido](https://zamborin.com/kaleido/): Stained-glass symmetry puzzle. A rose window with panes missing; no two panes of the same colour may touch, and that rule alone determines what belongs in every gap. You only edit one wedge and the rest of the window is its rotated copy, so one pane placed appears all the way round at once and must sit well with its neighbours in several places. 100 levels: the window grows, the symmetry loosens from six wedges to three to two, and more glass goes missing. Every gap has exactly one right answer, reachable by reasoning, never by guessing.
- [Untangle](https://zamborin.com/untangle/): Planar-graph puzzle. Drag the dots so no two edges cross. Endless levels from Tutorial to Master, each built from a fixed per-level seed, so a given level is the same board for everyone. Moves are counted against a par set by how many dots the generator moved.
- [Tessera](https://zamborin.com/tessera/): Endless falling-letter word puzzle. Tap a column to slide the tile; double-tap to drop it instantly. Form English words across or down, 3 letters minimum. Longer words score exponentially more. The game gets faster the longer you survive.
- [Sluice](https://zamborin.com/sluice/): Sliding pipe puzzle. A grid of pipe with a tap and a ring of flowers on the border. You never rotate a piece: you drag a whole row or column and it slides as one, wrapping around so what leaves one edge re-enters at the other. Rows and columns cross, so nothing can be fixed a piece at a time. One solution per board.
- [Fold](https://zamborin.com/fold/): Origami folding puzzle. Each level is a creased sheet carrying pairs of coloured marks — a solid dot and a matching ring. Tap a crease and the smaller flap folds over onto the rest of the sheet, flipping its marks and stacking them on the layer beneath. Solve by landing every dot on its ring. Undo steps back one fold at a time.
- [Mobile](https://zamborin.com/mobile/): Balancing-sculpture puzzle in the mid-century mobile style. Rods hang from rods; from their ends hang cut-paper shapes drawn from a tray. A rod is level when weight times arm length matches on both sides, so a heavy shape hung close in balances a light one hung far out. Weight is area, which means it is judged by eye rather than read off a number, and an unbalanced arm droops on its heavy side until corrected. Nothing to race and no way to lose.
- [Ballast](https://zamborin.com/ballast/): Merging and balancing game, and one of two Zamborin games with a score chase and a way to lose. A bowl stands on a ROUNDED base, so it rocks rather than sitting fixed. A claw on a chain drops orbs in; two orbs of the same size that come to rest touching fuse into one of the next size up, seven sizes in all, and the two largest cancel each other for a large bonus, which is the release valve that stops a strong run filling up with orbs that have nowhere to go. What makes it more than a merging game is that the bowl rocks on a curve, so its stability depends on HOW HIGH THE WEIGHT SITS rather than only which side it is on: below the base's radius of curvature the bowl rights itself, above it any offset runs away. Merging is the only thing that lowers the pile, so merging is how you stay upright and not merely how you score, and a run that is never tidied is lost even if it is never loaded to one side. The balance read-out is drawn ON the ground the bowl rocks on, green where it self-rights and red where it does not, with a tick showing where the current load is HEADED rather than where the lean has got to, so it warns roughly a second before the bowl moves. There is no landing prediction: the orb falls straight down but the release point belongs to the bowl and swings as it leans, so judging where a drop lands is the player's sum to do. Measured over 30 seeds, play that ignores balance topples about a quarter of runs and play that watches it topples none, scoring about 1.5x higher. Runs are reproducible from a seed. The physics is the same at every screen size, so a player cannot get an easier bowl on one platform.
- [Ricochet](https://zamborin.com/ricochet/): Ball-bouncing brick game, and the one Zamborin game with a score chase and a way to lose. A wall of numbered blocks descends one row a turn; the player drags to aim and releases a stream of balls that ricochet off the walls, the ceiling and the blocks until they settle back at the floor. The number on a block is the hits it still needs. The single decision is the aim angle and it is a large one: a lazy shot straight up collects four or five hits, while a shallow angle that rakes along under a row collects thirty, a gap of roughly five times that is visible while aiming. THE NEXT TURN FIRES FROM WHERE THE FIRST BALL CAME TO REST, so every turn has two outcomes, the damage done and the position inherited. Three other pieces share the board: mirrors, diagonal slabs that turn a ball ninety degrees and can be broken but cost several times a block, and which are what actually ends most runs because they never clear themselves; rocks, pale stone that never breaks but also never ends a run and simply rides off the bottom; and gold pickups that add a ball to the stream permanently, so one taken early compounds over the whole run. A read-out counts the turns remaining before the lowest piece crosses the red line. Runs are reproducible from a seed. The board is 7 columns on a phone and 17 on desktop, with ball growth scaled to width so both carry the same skill gradient, and a separate best score for each.
- [Tailwind](https://zamborin.com/tailwind/): Catapult distance game. A rubber-band slingshot mounted on a forked post flings an aeroplane, which climbs, settles into a glide, touches down and rolls to a stop; distance is counted where it stops. Three inputs, none of them dialled in: the first tap starts the band drawing back and a second tap fixes the force, then the whole catapult — band and aeroplane as one rigid piece — swings about its screw until a third tap releases, which fixes the launch angle. Once airborne the player has ONE burst of mid-air thrust, spent by tapping, and it is the largest single lever in the game: well timed it roughly doubles the throw. It is a timing decision rather than a free gift, because thrust is charged to the airframe in the same currency the launch is: the load of an impulse rises with the square of airspeed, so a boost fired while the aeroplane is still fast strains the wing and spends the glide, while the same boost fired slow costs almost nothing. The best moment therefore sits near the top of the climb where airspeed is lowest, and it MOVES with aircraft and wind rather than being one number to learn; a live airspeed read-out under the aeroplane is the cue. Both sweeps run fast enough that the good band is roughly 45-65 milliseconds wide, so knowing the right launch and landing it are separate skills. Six aircraft are offered, each showing weight, lift, drag and strength, and they are balanced to reach within a few per cent of the same distance by DIFFERENT launches rather than ranked. Reaching launch speed over a short stroke is a load of tens of g, so every airframe has a draw beyond which the wing strains and permanently loses lift and gains drag for that flight — the best draw runs from about half on the lightest to nearly full on the strongest. Aiming straight up loses, because the aeroplane arrives at the top with no flying speed and falls before it can glide. A wind is rolled fresh each attempt and shown on a dial before the player touches the band; its effect on the best angle is NOT monotonic: the best aim RISES as a headwind builds and peaks around 6 m/s, falls away through 7-11, and above about 11 flips to a low flat launch; a tailwind wants a slightly flatter aim than still air. It also changes which aircraft is fastest — light ones in calm air, heavy ones in a gale. A player who ignores the dial and repeats one still-air launch loses about an eighth of the distance on the worst days. Deterministic apart from the wind. A best distance is kept per aircraft.
- [Stained](https://zamborin.com/stained/): Colour-mixing glass puzzle. A dark window and a bench of translucent coloured panes, laid over each other so that where they overlap the colours mix. Mixing is PIGMENT, not light: red and yellow make orange, yellow and blue make green, blue and red make purple, all three make brown, and because a cell's colour is the union of the panes covering it, order never matters. The central decision is what the goal reveals: it shows ONLY the overlaps, meaning where colours must mix and what into, and hides the single-colour glass entirely. So a coloured square on the goal is a clue rather than an instruction, and everywhere else the player may do as they like provided they make no overlap that was not asked for. Some panes arrive already secondary and so carry two primaries at once, and the CAMPAIGN RAMP IS BUILT ON WITHDRAWING THEM: a secondary pane hands the player a mixed colour for free, so an orange cell can be satisfied with no crossing at all, and stripping them means every mixed cell must be earned by a real overlap. Fewer secondary panes therefore makes a board harder, not easier. A physical switch under the window lights it and falls dark a second after release, so checking your work is a deliberate act rather than a permanent view. 100 levels in 14 tiers, from a six by six window with two panes to an eight by eight with fifteen; each board's difficulty was measured individually and selected into its tier, so the ramp is monotone. Progress is kept in the browser. Every level is built by scrambling a solved arrangement, so a solution always exists.
- [Prism](https://zamborin.com/prism/): Light-routing colour puzzle. A lamp fires one white beam across a grid; a prism splits it into red, yellow and blue, but only for light arriving head on at its flat face, and light striking a slanted side is scattered and lost. Red carries straight on, yellow bends left, blue bends right. The board arrives EMPTY: the player is given a counted-out set of mirrors, which turn a beam ninety degrees, and splitters, which turn half of it and let the rest carry straight on so one beam becomes two. Deciding where to place them is the puzzle. Colours mix like pigment rather than light, so red and yellow make orange, red and blue make purple, and yellow and blue make green; a gem wanting a secondary needs two beams arriving at it together, and stays dark until both are right. Opaque blocks absorb any beam that reaches them. Every board is built around a working light path and re-simulated before it is served, so a solution always exists.
- [Needle](https://zamborin.com/needle/): Threading and crossing puzzle. Pairs of coloured pins sit on a cloth and each pair is joined by dragging its thread between them. The twist inverts the usual rule of the genre: threads are REQUIRED to cross rather than forbidden from it. A thread that meets nothing is lying on the surface, not sewn in, and is drawn drained of colour and floating above the cloth. Each thread must cross at least two others from level 3, one on levels 1 and 2. Each colour also has a single button its own thread must pass through, so the direct route is rarely the answer. A cell carries one horizontal pass and one vertical pass, which is what a crossing is; a thread that turns takes the whole cell. A Hint button lays one thread exactly where the answer puts it.
- [Zood](https://zamborin.com/zood/): Bubble-shooter arcade. Aim the cannon (mouse on desktop, drag on mobile) and fire character tiles at the cluster hanging above; match three or more of a kind to burst them, and any Zoods left dangling drop away too. Bank shots off the side walls to reach gaps you cannot hit head-on, and keep the cluster from reaching the line.
- [Carrom](https://zamborin.com/carrom/): Digital take on the South-Asian tabletop classic. Flick the striker, pocket your discs. Three difficulty levels against the computer.
- [Ludo](https://zamborin.com/ludo/): 2, 3, or 4-player Ludo board game. Roll one die, choose which of your four tokens to move, and capture opponents off the safe squares. A token leaves base on a six, which also earns another roll.

## Pages

- [Guides](https://zamborin.com/guides/): Strategy guides and how-to-play walkthroughs. One per game for Kaleido, Orbit, Bloom, Untangle, Tessera, Sluice, Fold, Mobile, Prism, Needle, Tailwind, Stained, Zood, Carrom and Ludo.
- [Embed](https://zamborin.com/embed/): How to put any Zamborin game on another website. One iframe, `?embed=1` on any game address, free for most sites, and the terms that go with it.
- [About](https://zamborin.com/about/): What Zamborin Games is and how the studio works.
- [FAQ](https://zamborin.com/faq/): Whether the games are free, whether an account is needed, mobile support, how the site makes money, and what data is collected.
- [Privacy](https://zamborin.com/privacy/): What data the site collects (almost none) and how Google AdSense cookies are used.
- [Contact](https://zamborin.com/contact/): Contact form for bug reports, feedback, partnerships.

## Background

The studio is run lean — small games shipped end-to-end by one or two people, no engine dependencies, no build pipeline. Every game is a folder of static HTML / JavaScript / CSS deployed via Vercel from a single git repository. Shared assets (audio engine, input helpers, design tokens) live in a `/shared/` toolkit.

The site is free to play and supported by Google AdSense. EU/UK/Switzerland visitors see a consent banner; everyone else sees ads without the prompt.
